title: 2real framework config
description: The single shared-config object every genericised framework artifact (hooks, libs, skills) reads. Installed at <repo>/.claude/framework.config.json by the bootstrapper. Nearly all fields are optional and fall back to the defaults documented here, so a minimal config is just {"version":1,"scm":{"provider":"github","owner":"my-org"}}.

version.description: Config schema version. Bumped only on a breaking change to this schema.

project.description: Human-facing identity of the project this config governs.

model.description: single-repo: one repository. meta-and-children: a parent meta-repo that .gitignores N child repos (the cross-repo orchestration model). child: one child repo inside a meta-and-children project — it carries NO hook code; its settings.json invokes the parent's installed hooks (see project.parent).

meta_repo.description: Name of the meta-repo (meta-and-children model only). The repo that holds the shared .claude/ config.

parent.description: Child model only: PORTABLE relative path from this repo's root to its parent meta-repo (e.g. `..` or `../..`). Never an absolute path — the whole meta tree stays cloneable anywhere.

flavor.description: Child model only: which hook events this child wires to the parent's dispatchers. product = the full harness; infra = the commit-safety + CI subset (pre/post Bash only; no ontology/session extras).

repos.description: Repos in scope (meta-and-children model). Bare names, resolved under scm.owner. Single-repo projects omit this.

scm.description: Source-control + host provider settings. Read by every git/gh-aware hook and lib.

provider.description: Only github is implemented today; the field exists so a future provider (gitlab, …) is a config change, not a code fork.

owner.description: GitHub org or user that owns the repo(s). Used to qualify bare repo names and gh calls.

allow_force.description: When false, force-push / force-merge guards are active.

branch.description: Branch-name grammar. Tokens in braces are substituted by the skills/hooks that mint or validate branches.

integration.description: Wave/iteration integration branch (meta-and-children / wave model). Tokens: {phase} {wave}.

board.description: Planning-board (GitHub Projects v2) settings. Omit the whole block if the project does not use a board.

project_number.description: GitHub Projects v2 number under scm.owner.

wave_field.description: Single-select field name the wave label projects onto.

identity.description: Commit-identity convention. Read by the commit-identity hooks and the trust/roster libs.

enforce.description: When true, per-commit identity is validated against the roster + email pattern.

roster_source.description: Path (repo-relative) to the roster manifest the identity hooks read.

allow_emails.description: Bare author emails accepted without matching the persona pattern (e.g. the owner).

policy.description: Process policy knobs read by the PR / merge / review gates.

reviewers_required.description: Approving reviewers required before merge (the N-reviewer gate).

pr_review_gate_enabled.description: Arms the validate_pr_review PreToolUse gate (#195). When true, `gh pr ready`/`gh pr merge` is BLOCKED unless lib/pr_review_state reports the PR is approved (approvals >= reviewers_required AND no unresolved Must-fix). Defaults false: the gate SHIPS DORMANT (a no-op ALLOW) so installing it never blocks a merge; activation is a deliberate opt-in.

merge_model.description: Per-iteration merge model. wave-branch: PRs base on the integration branch, integration PR at wrapup. direct-to-main: PRs base on the default branch.

admin_merge_exceptions.description: Map of <class> -> <human rationale> naming the only admin-merge bypass classes the CI gate accepts via ADMIN_MERGE_EXCEPTION=<class>:<rationale>. Empty = no admin bypass allowed.

default.refactor: Pure refactor / no external behavior change (renames, extraction, dead-code removal, formatting) - nothing new to test. State exactly what was restructured and confirm no observable behavior changed.
default.docs: Pure documentation / comment diff (docstring or comment-only additions, no new/changed executable statement) - nothing new to test. Applied automatically per behavior file (#284) when every added line in that file's diff is docstring/comment content; state exactly what was documented if invoking the manual override instead.

load_bearing_test_exceptions.description: Map of <class> -> <human rationale> naming the bypass classes the load-bearing-test pre-review gate (require_load_bearing_test.py, #167) accepts via LOAD_BEARING_TEST_EXCEPTION=<class>:<rationale> on `gh pr create`/`gh pr ready`. Ships pre-seeded with a `refactor` class (#176) so a pure-refactor PR is not hard-blocked with zero configured bypass, and a `docs` class (#284) which ALSO arms an automatic PER-FILE exemption (no env var needed) for a behavior file whose entire diff is docstring/comment content; a repo may add more classes.

tech_debt_intake_pct.description: Per-wave tech-debt intake: after a wave's feature/bug/security content is set, /plan-phase allocates tech-debt-only issues equal to this percentage of that content (rounded up). A cap on every wave except the last wave of a phase, where it becomes a floor.

tech_debt_exit_ratio_pct.description: Phase exit gate: maximum percentage of tech-debt issues (new-filed during the phase, and cumulative-open) tolerated at phase exit. /phase-review flags the gate as NOT MET at or above this.

retro_counter_drift_abs.description: /wave-retro counter-drift tolerance (absolute). A wrapup-recorded counter differing from the retro recomputation within this absolute diff OR within retro_counter_drift_pct percent is corrected and logged; a drift exceeding both is a retro-blocker.

branch_freshness_max_commits_behind.description: validate_branch_freshness.py (#179): when > 0, a feature branch is flagged once it is behind its base by MORE than this many commits. 0 (default) DISABLES the commits-behind dimension — branch-freshness is opt-in, off by default (0 == disabled, matching branch_freshness_max_age_days; NOT zero-tolerance). With both freshness knobs 0 the gate does nothing (no git/gh call).

branch_freshness_max_age_days.description: validate_branch_freshness.py (#179): additionally flag a branch whose merge-base with its base branch is older than this many days (only evaluated when the branch is already behind by at least one commit). 0 (default) disables the age dimension — only branch_freshness_max_commits_behind is enforced.

merge_requires_green.description: Block gh pr merge when the PR's statusCheckRollup is failing/pending.

empty_rollup_is_blocking.description: Treat an empty statusCheckRollup as not-ready (subject to the covering-workflow discriminator). 'No checks reported' is not the same as green.

neutral_pending_check_prefixes.description: CheckRun display-name prefixes whose NEUTRAL conclusion means 'review pending' (treated as pending), not 'no opinion' (treated as pass). E.g. ['chromatic'].

tooling.description: The complete CI check-set (linters/formatters/type/test/spell/…) the local<->CI parity gate expects mirrored in pre-commit. E.g. ['ruff','mypy','pytest'].

shell.description: The dev/agent shell. When 'zsh', the zsh-wordsplit safety warner is meaningful (bash-isms that silently break under zsh).

paths.description: Repo-relative locations of framework artifacts. Defaults match the bootstrap install layout.

team.description: Charter + roster + trust matrix + feedback log.

state_file.description: The wave/iteration state file the lifecycle skills read/write.

events_log.description: Where hooks append block/event records (the generic observability stream).

generic_prompt_ledger.description: The durable per-artifact genericize/skip decision ledger (#102) the suggest_generic_prompt hook feeds and the promotion-audit skill reads.

promotion_audit_log.description: Directory the promotion-audit skill writes its per-wave audit log into (wave_<id>.md).

hooks.description: The dispatcher seam: which hook modules are active and in what order. The bootstrapper writes this; editing it enables/disables checks without touching code. Names are module names under .claude/hooks/ (no .py).

pre_bash.description: Ordered PreToolUse/Bash checks. Cheap/local first, network-calling (gh) last. First block wins.

post_bash.description: Ordered PostToolUse/Bash checks. Advisory only — never block.

post_file.description: Ordered PostToolUse checks for file-mutating tools (Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit). Advisory only — never block.

session_start.description: Ordered SessionStart checks (run via start_dispatcher.py). Advisory only — never block; INERT unless the subsystem they target exists (e.g. ontology_refresh acts only when an ontology dir is present; session_start only orients when a framework config is found).

agent.description: Ordered PreToolUse checks for the Agent tool (subagent spawns; settings matcher `Agent`, legacy name `Task`). Same semantics as pre_bash: first block wins. Empty by default — the dispatch seam ships wired so enabling a check is a config edit, not settings surgery.

stop.description: Ordered Stop-event checks (run via stop_dispatcher.py). Advisory only — NEVER block (a block decision is downgraded to a warning). Each must be cheap/no-op when there is nothing to do; session_handoff throttles itself and never overwrites a manual /handoff note.

pre_push_commands.description: Shell commands the ENFORCE-mode pre-push git hook runs (in order, from the repo root) before every push; the first nonzero exit blocks the push. Read at push time, so editing this list needs no reinstall. Empty = the enforce hook allows the push (fail-open). Ignored by the default noop hook. Installed via bootstrap.py --pre-push {noop,enforce,none}.
